title: Contractivity of the noise operator in $L^2$
statement:
Fix $n$, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be any Boolean function, and let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2\le 1$. Writing $T_\rho$ for the noise operator, so that $T_\rho f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$, one has
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big]\;\le\;\E\big[f^2\big],
\]
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is an arbitrary Boolean function of arity n
replaced:
For $\rho^2 \le 1$ and any Boolean function $f$,
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^2] \le \E[f^2].
\]
This is the $q = 2$ case of hypercontractivity.
